summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with left-sided chest pain that began the prior night and was positional—relieved by sitting up and recurring when lying down. Given his history of coronary artery disease and prior bypass surgery, he was evaluated for acute myocardial infarction and pulmonary embolism. Initial troponin was slightly elevated but unchanged from baseline, and repeat testing showed no rise. EKG revealed no new ischemic changes, and D-dimer was normal, ruling out PE. Chest imaging showed stable atelectasis and pleural calcifications from prior asbestos exposure, but no acute cardiopulmonary pathology. The pain resolved in the emergency department and did not recur. The episode was not cardiac in origin, and psychogenic or positional causes were considered most likely. He was discharged home with instructions to follow up with his primary care provider for a stress test, medication adjustments, and ongoing management of chronic conditions including diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, depression, and neurogenic bladder requiring an indwelling Foley catheter.
